descriptionAdvanced.en: The Bioceanic Highway (Corredor Bioceánico) is a strategic international transit route that serves as a modern 'Panama Canal on land,' connecting the Brazilian Atlantic port of Santos with the Chilean Pacific ports of Iquique and Arica. In Bolivia, the highway traverses the vast eastern lowlands of Santa Cruz and the rugged Andean highlands, acting as the primary artery for the country's import and export economy. It has been a key driver for the agricultural expansion in the Chiquitania region and provides a vital link for the transit of goods between the world's major economies in Asia and the productive heart of South America. The completion of this corridor has significantly reduced transport times and costs, positioning Bolivia as a crucial logistical hub for the entire continent.

en: The Bolivian section of the highway stretches for over 1,500 kilometers.
It is a cornerstone of the Integration of the Regional Infrastructure of South America (IIRSA).
The highway passes through important eco-regions like the Pantanal and the Chiquitano dry forest.
It facilitates the export of massive volumes of Brazilian soy and Bolivian minerals to world markets.
